business_scope.primary_industry_name: GPS-Sealed Bonded Road Feeder Service for International Airports

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Government of the French Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 1984, entered into force 1985)
Convention between France and the United States of America with respect to taxes on income and capital, together with related protocols (signed 1994, entered into force 1995)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied since 21 September 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 et seq. and R.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Article L.561-2-1 as inserted by Ordinance No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 on the register of beneficial owners; Decree No. 2020-1747 of 29 December 2020; Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin 2); FATF Recommendations as implemented.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of shareholder's passport or national identity card
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent embassy/consulate in shareholder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of registration, articles of association and certificate of good standing of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry (e.g., Companies House for UK, Hong Kong Companies Registry, Singapore ACRA)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration / mandat) appointing the French local representative and/or proposed SARL manager (gérant)
Police clearance certificate (casier judiciaire bulletin nº3 equivalent) for each individual shareholder, manager and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French casier judiciaire national or equivalent foreign criminal records authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, proposed managers, authorised signatories and beneficial owners against the consolidated EU financial sanctions list, the French national sanctions list (FCPI/Ministry of Economy), the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, and FATF high-risk jurisdictions; enhanced PEP screening is required under Article L.561-10 of the Monetary and Financial Code. OFAC screening is also performed for USD-denominated wire transactions, subject to the EU Blocking Regulation (Council Regulation (EC) No 2271/96) as applicable to French legal entities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet des formalités des entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); RCS record search is performed via Infogreffe (infogreffe.eu).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French law requires the company name (dénomination sociale) to be expressed in French or, where a foreign-language term is used, accompanied by a French translation where the name may be misleading. Non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic) must be transliterated into Latin characters for RCS registration; the registrar may require a certified transliteration document. Doctrine source: Article L.121-1 of the French Consumer Code (Loi n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994, known as the Loi Toubon) and commercial registry practice.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANQUE / BANK (requires prior authorization from the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority, ACPR)
ASSURANCE / INSURANCE (requires prior authorization from ACPR)
ÉTAT / NATIONAL (requires prior ministerial authorization where it may mislead as to official capacity)
FRANCE / RÉPUBLIQUE / COMMUNAUTÉ (requires prior ministerial approval where the name may falsely suggest public affiliation)
AVOCAT / NOTAIRE / OFFICIER MINISTÉRIEL (reserved for regulated legal professions)
CHAMBRE DE COMMERCE / COMMISSAIRE / HUISSIER (regulated professional title usage restrictions)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce) rejects the proposed company name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal (recours gracieux) with the same greffe within 15 days of notification of rejection. If the administrative appeal is refused, the applicant may apply to the judge supervising the Register of Commerce and Companies (juge commis à la surveillance du Registre du commerce et des sociétés) within 15 days of the second rejection. Where refusal is based on a prior trademark or company name conflict, the applicant may also contest the registration decision before the Presiding Judge of the Tribunal judiciaire in summary proceedings (référé).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office (domiciliation) is generally accepted for a French SARL under Articles L.123-11-1 and R.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code, provided the virtual office is operated by an approved domiciliation company and the statutory seat is compliant with local zoning rules. However, for a customs bonded road feeder trucking operation under ISIC 5222, the operator must maintain a physical operational base in France, obtain a transport operator licence (licence communautaire) under Regulation (EC) No 1072/2009, and be approved by the French customs authority (DGDDI) for bonded transportation; a purely virtual office will not satisfy these operational requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (quantified risk: approximately 75% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months) because bonded trucking operations and customs licensed facilities are subject to unannounced checks by DGDDI customs officers, DREAL transport inspectors and the operational road transport police (OPTR).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed-fee or hourly legal fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the statutory formation notice in a journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Official legal notice journal (JAL) publisher of record
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by arrêté préfectoral per the amount of share capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration fee and formalities processing through the Guichet unique (INPI / greffe du tribunal de commerce)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by the French Ministry of Justice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the beneficial owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) filed with the RCS/RBE register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / Registre du commerce et des sociétés

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and availability verification across RCS, BODACC, PIB (detailed database) and INPI trademark databases
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory search tariff plus prevailing market benchmark for legal opinion

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign shareholder, manager and UBO documents (standard bundle of four documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority and/or foreign consulate in country of document origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing consular and apostille fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, sanctions, and adverse media screening of all UBOs, managers and signatories in line with French AML/CFT law
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML/KYC compliance technology provider and independent legal review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark subscription and per-file screening fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title III, Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 et seq.; registration formalities under Articles L.123-1 to L.123-12 and R.123-1 et seq.; SARL formation implemented through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), transmitting the dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) of the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution de société (formerly form M0/CERFA 13928) filed electronically on the Guichet Unique, accompanied by the signed statuts, the blocked-capital deposit certificate, and the Journal d'Annonces Légales publication certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital for an SARL; capital is set freely in the articles. Cash capital must be fully subscribed and at least 20% of each cash contribution must be paid up before registration, with the balance payable within five years; in-kind capital must be fully paid up immediately. The cash contribution is placed in a blocked escrow account with a credit institution, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts, and the depositary certificate is attached to the RCS filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each subscriber confirms the acceptance of the shares set opposite his name and confirms that the share capital of EUR 1,000 has been fully subscribed and, to the extent required by law, paid up into a blocked account, all in accordance with Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code. RESOLVED, that the articles of association are adopted as presented and that the registered office is fixed at [address], Paris, for legal and administrative purposes. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as first Gérant for an indefinite period, with full powers to represent, bind and operate the company, to complete all registration formalities, to open bank accounts, and to file and maintain all customs bonded transport, operational and environmental permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) and RCS database via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an availability search of the proposed SARL name, trademark register, and RCS registered names to confirm there is no conflicting legal entity. Record search results in the formation file. If the name is clear, proceed to drafting; if not, select an alternative name and re-run the search. The final name is fixed in the articles and acquires priority upon submission of the M0 declaration.
required_dossiers: Summary of corporate object corresponding to ISIC 5222
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a conflict is identified, amend the company name, add a distinctive suffix, or withdraw and resubmit alternatives before the formal filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of French Statutory Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All shareholders executing either private deed or notarial deed; a notaire is mandatory where real-property contributions are made.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French containing the SARL corporate form, company name, registered office, share capital, division into parts sociales, corporate purpose limited to customs bonded road feeder services and ancillary activities, duration, first Gérant, and decision and control rules. Execute the statuts by all shareholders in as many originals as required by law, each party retaining one original. If any contribution in kind is made, complete the valuation report and have the commissaire aux apports confirm assets before execution.
required_dossiers: Lease or occupancy title for the registered office
In-kind contribution valuation report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notaire or registry queries a clause, execute an amending rider or re-sign corrected articles before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Deposit and Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Credit institution, notaire escrow, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the SARL being formed. Deposit the full cash capital or, where the articles validly provide, at least the one-fifth minimum required by law for such cash contribution and obtain the certificate du dépositaire des fonds showing the exact amount and that the funds are frozen until registration. In-kind contributions must be entirely transferred and valued at their real value before the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Commissaire aux apports report, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the depositary refuses the certificate, verify legal form and beneficiary details, correct the account title, and re-submit the deposit instruction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Incorporation Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorised by the prefecture of the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Insert a notice in the JAL containing the SARL corporate form, company name, share capital, registered office, corporate object, term, name of the gérant and the RCS jurisdiction. Pay the publication fee and obtain the certificate of publication indicating the date of the insertion and the JAL reference.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is refused or corrected, publish an amended notice immediately and retain both notices for the RCS file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Centralised Filing and RCS Registration through the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI portal); transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the M0 declaration in French, attach all required scans, validate the proposed NAF/APE code corresponding to ISIC 5222, and pay the fixed greffe fee. Submit the dossier online and track the electronic status. The Guichet Unique routes the dossier to the RCS, INSEE for SIREN/SIRET, and the competent social and fiscal administrations. Upon approval, the SARL is registered and the Kbis extract becomes available.
required_dossiers: M0 declaration form via Guichet Unique
Proof of registered office and occupancy right
Identity and address certificate of the Gérant
Notarised power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is flagged as incomplete, correct and resubmit through the Guichet Unique within the time limit stated in the electronic notification; after a final refusal, petition by application to the President of the Commercial Court for a registration order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS and INSEE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the official Kbis extract after registration; verify SIREN, SIRET, legal form, capital, registered office, gérant, company object, and the assigned French NAF code. Order certified copies where required for bank account opening, customs bond registration, and client airport vetting. Obtain the separate INSEE attestation if available in the online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains errors, file a rectification request with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and confirm the corrected entries before relying on the extract.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires, represented by the Préfet de Région and DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement); customs authorisations issued by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence de transport routier intérieur de marchandises (licence communautaire for intra-EU movements) and, for the customs bonded regime, status of authorised consignor / authorised consignee under NCTS T1 transit, together with an Operateur Economique Agréé (AEOS) or equivalent customs simplification where required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement, Inspection des Installations Classées (ICPE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA for a pure airport road feeder operation without fixed installations; however, any covered warehouse, maintenance facility, or fuel depot will require ICPE declaration or registration, typically under rubrique 1510 for dry storage and rubrique 2910 for combustion installations if applicable.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge into public sewers must comply with Code de l'Environnement and the local prefectoral wastewater order; solvent and VOC emissions from any maintenance or degreasing activity must comply with French solvent management thresholds and Directive 2004/42/EC volatile organic compound limits; hazard waste handling must satisfy Articles R.541-2 et seq. of the Code de l'Environnement; HGV fleet engines must meet Euro VI and Crit'Air standards applicable to the Paris airport zone.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate or inspection receipt from the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) for any covered vehicle bay or auxiliary premises; structural load inspection certificate for warehouses, loading docks and parking decks; occupational health and safety registration with CARSAT, completion of a Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), compliance with working time rules, use of certified equipment, and pre-start safety clearance for fuel storage and vehicle maintenance areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP), the French national tax authority; online portal: impots.gouv.fr (professional access for VAT, CIT and withholding filings). Business incorporation and tax ID registration are filed through the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by INPI at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Customs and bonded-transit matters are handled by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), including AEO (Opérateur Économique Agréé) and NCTS T1/T2 transit authorizations. Non-resident entities registering for VAT deal with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE) in Montreuil.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL: (1) file statutory incorporation documents (statuts, registered-office proof, gérant identity) through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; (2) the CFE/INPI transmits the dossier to INSEE for allocation of the 9-digit SIREN and 14-digit SIRET; (3) DGFIP automatically issues the 13-character intra-Community VAT number (format FR + 2 control digits + 9-digit SIREN) upon completion of registration; (4) register as employer with URSSAF if hiring staff; (5) if bonded customs operations are intended, obtain an AEO/Customs transit authorization from DGDDI. For a foreign entity without a French establishment: no turnover threshold applies; the entity must file CERFA Form No. 16782 (demande d'attribution d'un numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) with the SIEE in Montreuil, provide the foreign TIN and proof of business existence, and appoint a French fiscal representative (représentant fiscal assujetti) jointly and severally liable for VAT where French VAT registrations are required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a French SARL is by default subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS) at entity level, at 25% above €42,500 of taxable profit and 15% on the first €42,500 for eligible SMEs (≤€7.6 million turnover, capital fully paid up, at least 75% held by individuals). Territorial_Scope: France applies the territoriality principle, so profits attributable to a foreign permanent establishment are outside the French IS charge (CGI 209). Tax_Exempt_Zone: no general tax-exempt zone applies to airport feeder trucking; only very narrow ZFU/urban free-zone incentives exist and are not relevant here.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1. Check-the-box-style option for pass-through taxation: a SARL with more than 50% of its capital held directly by natural persons may elect, under CGI Article 239 ter AA, to be taxed as a transparent partnership (régime des sociétés de personnes) for 5 fiscal years, renewable, provided the option is filed within the first 3 months of the starting fiscal year. 2. Family SARL election: all shareholders within the family circle may keep the IR (income-tax) regime indefinitely, and may conversely elect for IS. 3. Tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under CGI Article 223 A: a 95%+ parent may consolidate French subsidiaries for IS. 4. Hybrid mismatch: France has no entity-level check-the-box election; ATAD (Directive (EU) 2016/1164 as amended by (EU) 2017/952) hybrid mismatch rules are implemented through the Finance Act 2019, disallowing deductions for deductible-without-includible payments and double-deduction arrangements, and applying anti-reverse-hybrid treatment to certain French-resident entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French value added tax, implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC); supplemented for customs-bonded trucking by the EU customs union rules (NCTS T1/T2 transit, ICS2, bonded warehouse regime). Road freight transport services supplied in France are taxable at the standard VAT rate; intra-Community and export-related movements are governed by the place-of-supply and reverse-charge mechanisms.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For French-established taxable persons, the 'franchise en base de TVA' exemption (CGI 293 B) relieves the taxpayer from VAT registration when preceding-year taxable turnover does not exceed €36,800 for services (including road freight transport) or €91,900 for supplies of goods, and projected current-year turnover does not exceed €39,100 or €101,000 respectively; crossing those ceilings triggers compulsory DGFIP registration. For non-established foreign entities, VAT registration is compulsory from the first euro of taxable supplies performed in France with no threshold. For a B2B road-feeder carrier, the reverse charge on intra-Community transport services and on supplies by non-resident providers avoids a local VAT registration unless the entity maintains a fixed establishment in France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France implements the mandatory e-invoicing/e-reporting reform (Loi de finances pour 2023, Ordonnance 2022-1087): from 1 September 2026, all French taxable persons must be able to receive structured electronic invoices, and large/mid-size enterprises must issue e-invoices (Factur-X or UBL 2.1/cXML) and transmit standardized e-invoice and e-transaction data to the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF/Chorus Pro) directly or via certified Partner Dematerialisation Platforms (PDPs); from 1 September 2027, SMEs and micro-enterprises (including typical SARLs) must issue and transmit as well. The architecture is a 'cocktail model' of interconnection and central storage at the PPF, not real-time per-invoice fiscal stamping, but DGFIP receives transactional data within prescribed 10-day reporting windows and reconciles invoices electronically. Paper invoices lose tax validity for B2B supplies. On the customs side, export declarations and T1/T2 transit movements are fully electronic through DELTA-D/ NSTI and the EU Trader Portal with ICS2 Entry Summary declarations; GPS-sealed trailers must match the transit accompanying document and the customs office of exit in order for the zero-rating to be sustained.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to export supplies of goods (CGI Article 262-I) and to services directly linked to the export operation, including transport, handling, loading and customs formalities (CGI Article 262-II), provided: (a) the goods physically leave EU customs territory within 90 days from supply/invoicing; (b) the exporter is VAT-registered and holds a valid export customs declaration (DAU) with the EXS 'Goods Released' outcome from DELTA-D; (c) the transport is evidenced by CMR, Air Waybill/Master Air Waybill or Bill of Lading clearly identifying the goods, the exporter/importer, gross weight, HS codes and the customs office of exit; (d) consideration is receivable and export proceeds are repatriated within the statutory 180-day FX deadline; and (e) for the GPS-sealed bonded road-feeder service, the cargo movement is supervised under a T1/T2 or TIR transit procedure, with the airport hub as an authorized customs-bonded facility and the final non-EU destination proven by inbound-control records. Domestic trucking legs within France that are not part of a documented export movement remain taxable at 20%; refunds of excess input VAT on zero-rated exports may be claimed monthly via the 'remboursement de crédit de TVA' procedure on impots.gouv.fr.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU — Document Administratif Unique) lodged electronically in the DELTA-D export module, showing the MRN, the EXS 'Goods Released' status and, where applicable, the NCTS T1/T2 transit movement reference for the bonded truck fleet.

Transport and Transit Documents: CMR consignment note (road feeder fleet), Air Waybill/Master Air Waybill (airport hub), or multimodal Bill of Lading, together with the customs transit accompanying document (TAD), the sealed-truck GPS manifest and the outward-office exit certificate (attestation de sortie).

Inward Remittance Certificate: French bank certificate of export-proceeds collection (certificat de domiciliation bancaire) or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt in EUR of the export sale within the 180-day deadline, matched to the commercial invoice and the exporter's accounts.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFIP and DGDDI jointly verify export zero-rating claims by cross-referencing the export declaration (EXS), the NCTS transit closure and the bank receipts of foreign currency. Unsupported or falsely documented exports are recharacterized as domestic supplies subject to 20% VAT, triggering a 'rappel de TVA' for up to 3 prior fiscal years (extended to 6 years for fraudulent omission or 10 years for hidden activity), plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month (intérêts de retard). Standard penalties: 40% of the reassessed VAT for deliberate insufficiency (CGI 1731), 80% for bad faith or fraudulent maneuvers (CGI 1729), and 100% for abuse of law or use of false documents; aggravated criminal tax fraud (CGI 1741) carries up to 5 years' imprisonment and a €500,000 fine (up to 7 years and €750,000 in organized-fraud form); customs penalties under Code des douanes include fines of 1 to 5 times the defrauded duties, confiscation of the truck and cargo, and suspension or withdrawal of AEO and bonded-warehouse authorizations. The SARL's gérant is jointly and severally liable and may face personal criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) — acting in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for exchange-control policy and capital-flow regulation, and with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for banking conduct and AML supervision. The Banque de France administers balance-of-payments (BOP) statistical reporting through its GABARI reporting system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: EUR is fully convertible under Article 63 TFEU (free movement of capital). Current-account transactions are deregulated; capital-account transactions are also liberalized, subject only to the French declarative reporting regime (régime déclaratif) for cross-border flows exceeding statistical thresholds. Profit remittance requires no exchange-control authorization, but remains subject to the SARL statutory reserve rule (appropriation of at least 10% of annual profits until 5% of share capital is reached) and to domestic or treaty-based dividend withholding exposure for non-resident shareholders.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender obligation applies to French-resident exporters. Foreign-currency export receipts may be retained, converted, or transferred freely. However, every payment transaction with a non-resident of an amount equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000 must be reported automatically by the servicing bank to Banque de France for BOP statistics via the GABARI return; the corporate client must maintain the underlying transport, customs-bonded, and invoicing records for audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Bloqué) / Operational Account (Compte Courant)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole (including LCL and regional Caisses)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for routine operational accounts and cross-border payment execution via ACPR-licensed or EEA-passported electronic money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Revolut Business) under PSD2. Fee levels, FX spreads, and API-driven treasury management are commercially attractive. Low for statutory capital-escrow perfection because the blocked-deposit certificate required for SARL incorporation must be issued by a credit institution or a notary. Non-EEA offshore digital EMIs have Low viability: without an EU EMI licence and AML/CFT registration in France, they cannot lawfully provide payment services to the French entity nor access national clearing systems.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one gérant (legal representative) is ordinarily expected to appear physically at the bank branch for the initial signature-card execution (spécimen de signature) and for perfection of the capital-blocked deposit certificate. The ACPR framework permits remote video-identification under the DDPI (Digital Identity) standard, and several Tier-1 banks offer hybrid onboarding for low-risk professional clients such as GPS-sealed bonded trucking. A physical interview remains recommended for first non-EU shareholder resolutions and for any high-value capital injection. Remote opening alone is not universally accepted for the blocked capital account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership chain opaque or inconsistent with the RBE filing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extrait Kbis (issued within 3 months), certified statutes and share register, Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) confirmation, corporate-organisation chart, beneficial-owner passports and proof of residence, and a signed beneficial-ownership attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of share-capital contribution (apport en capital) not fully evidenced
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contributing shareholder's bank statements, gift or sale deeds, previous tax notices, notarial capital-holding certificate, blocked-funds certificate issued by the depositary bank, and sworn declaration on the lawful origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate existence or gérant authority documentation incomplete
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificat d'immatriculation (Kbis), copy of public incorporation announcements, notarized or witnessed statutes, banking resolution of partners, powers of attorney (pouvoirs), gérant identity document, and partner register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors' tax domicile or economic link to France unclear
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French avis d'imposition or French tax-residence certificate, address and/or lease verification, CRS and FATCA self-certification for each non-resident shareholder, explanation of the French operational substance (customs-bonded truck fleet, airport contracts).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire rationale or counterparty sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed transport and airport-services contracts, cargo manifests and customs-bonded movement reports, proforma supplier invoices, sanctions-screening clearance, and a written treasury mandate describing the commercial purpose of each wire.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share-capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 pacs.008 in straight-through Euro clearing) to the dedicated blocked capital account, using purpose code 'EQUI' and the Remittance Information field stating 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION – SARL INCORPORATION'. Where the inbound remitter is non-resident and the amount exceeds EUR 50,000, the receiving bank files the automatic BOP declaration through GABARI; the client must retain the blocked-funds certificate, notarized contribution minutes, and source-of-funds evidence for verification. For creditor-company contributions, the routing must match the share issuance resolution and capital increase procedure.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements in EUR are executed through SEPA Credit Transfer/TARGET2 (direct ACH-Direct rails). Non-EUR supplier and fuel disbursements use SWIFT MT103 with commercially reviewed remittance data. High-value fleet, truck, or aviation-equipment purchases from international OEMs should be settled under a UCP600-compliant documentary commercial letter of credit (confirmed or unconfirmed), with presentation of transport documents and GPS-sealed cargo reports. Bank Payment Obligation (BPO) may be used where supplier banks support the ISO 20022 matching utility. Clearing discipline requires dual-step operator confirmation for every outbound transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD and EUR/GBP outright currency forwards (change à terme) with ACPR-authorized credit institutions under the FBF standard master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on currencies without liquid domestic spot delivery, covering emerging-market transport and fuel corridors
Cross-currency swaps (swaps de change) for refinancing or term-asset hedging, executed subject to EMIR clearing, margining, and eligibility thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements approval and filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; commercial court registry through the INPI single business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval within six months after financial year-end; filing within one month after approval, or two months for electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and daily penalty payments may apply; the managing director may face a statutory fine of approximately EUR 1,500, doubled for repetition. No fixed automatic strike-off period applies solely for late accounts, but prolonged inactivity or non-compliance may lead to registry removal or dissolution procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration through the professional tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company; generally within three months after year-end for other closing dates, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a 10% penalty, late-payment interest, estimated assessment, and additional penalties for inaccuracies or non-payment. No automatic corporate strike-off is triggered solely by a late tax return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and management report approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; no routine filing authority unless a specific resolution or filing is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after financial year-end, ordinarily before approval and filing of the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve accounts may support a court order, director liability exposure, and late or non-filing sanctions. No automatic strike-off deadline applies solely because the annual meeting is late.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI single business formalities portal and competent commercial court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven; update generally within 30 days after a change in beneficial ownership or the reported information. France does not generally require a separate annual confirmation where no change occurred.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain accurate beneficial ownership information may result in a court injunction and criminal penalties, including a fine of up to EUR 7,500 and imprisonment of up to six months for the responsible individual. No automatic annual strike-off timeline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT returns and annual VAT reconciliation, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration through the professional tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly CA3 returns under the normal regime; annual VAT return under the simplified regime, generally with the applicable annual return deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment may trigger a 10% penalty, late-payment interest, estimated assessment, and penalties for under-declaration. No automatic corporate strike-off is triggered solely by late VAT filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Road freight operator licence and transport compliance renewal review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Regional prefecture or competent regional transport authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Licence validity and renewal dates are licence-specific; annual internal review should confirm financial standing, professional competence, vehicle documentation, insurance, and operator details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without valid authorisation may result in administrative suspension or withdrawal, fines, vehicle immobilisation, and transport-law penalties. This is not an annual corporate registry filing and has no automatic corporate strike-off timetable.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for a SARL exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Separate group-company rules may apply to parent companies, subsidiaries, or entities controlled by another company.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority rules is generally required for standalone statutory accounts. IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts or where legally permitted; it is not the default framework for standalone SARL accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO confirmation is generally required in France if the filed information remains unchanged. The SARL must monitor ownership, control, management, and address data continuously and file amendments promptly, generally within 30 days. Share transfers must be documented in the applicable transfer instrument, shareholder records, and corporate approvals.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or share-transfer records
Register of Directors and corporate officers
Minute Book containing shareholders' and management resolutions
Beneficial ownership records and filed declarations
Accounting books, supporting records, and annual financial statements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,000-15,000 per year for a small or medium SARL, depending on turnover, fleet size, group reporting, internal controls, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Eligible small companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory conditions, including annual turnover generally not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% ownership by individuals or qualifying entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: France has no general corporate tax holiday for a standard SARL conducting bonded airport feeder trucking. Available incentives may include the 15% small-company rate, qualifying research and development tax credits, certain regional investment incentives, and sector-specific deductions or credits where statutory conditions are met. Dividends received by a qualifying French parent may benefit from the participation exemption, generally with a 5% taxable share; the share may be reduced to 1% for certain qualifying tax-group situations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire No. 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, with the applicable 2065-SD annexes and tax tables, filed electronically through the French tax administration professional portal or by EDI-TDFC through an authorized intermediary.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly corporate tax installments are generally payable during the year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the normal deadline is the second business day after 1 May of the following year. Corporate tax installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December; the final balance is generally due on the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, with a special timetable for 31 December year-ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, SIREN, SIRET, legal form, principal activity, fiscal year dates, and contact details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the French permanent establishment, branch, or subsidiary details. A non-resident shareholder is not substituted for the French SARL as the filing taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Corporate tax regime and fiscal period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate liability to impôt sur les sociétés, fiscal year opening and closing dates, and applicable tax consolidation or group-election information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SARL's own fiscal period and identify any French tax group or foreign-parent relationship where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report accounting profit or loss adjusted for non-deductible expenses, exempt income, tax depreciation differences, provisions, and other French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and expenses legally attributable to the French taxable entity or French permanent establishment. Apply arm's-length pricing to dealings with foreign related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose tax losses carried forward or carried back and the amount utilized in the current period, subject to statutory utilization limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign group losses are not automatically deductible by the French SARL. Document French ownership, tax-group, and restructuring conditions before using losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 25% standard rate, any eligible 15% small-company rate, applicable credits, foreign tax relief, and prior payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes are not automatically creditable. Apply the relevant treaty, domestic limitation, and documentary requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report qualifying tax credits, including research and development credits or other specifically available statutory incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain French supporting records and substantiate qualifying expenditure, personnel, assets, and business activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile installments, withholding amounts, credits, and the final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments must be made through the designated French professional tax account or approved electronic payment channel.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report required related-party transaction information and submit or make available transfer-pricing documentation where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border management fees, freight arrangements, financing, guarantees, royalties, procurement, and centralized-service charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report dividends, interest, royalties, salaries, or other payments subject to French withholding obligations and related remittances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty relief only after verifying beneficial ownership, residence documentation, anti-abuse conditions, and any required form or refund process.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide balance sheet, profit-and-loss, fixed-asset, depreciation, provisions, and other tax-table information required by the 2065-SD package.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign accounting records must be reconciled to French statutory accounts and translated or supported sufficiently for French tax inspection.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and potentially 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive concealment. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Additional fixed or percentage penalties may apply for missing annexes, inaccurate information, tax withholding failures, or transfer-pricing documentation failures.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic French withholding tax on dividends paid to a non-resident corporate recipient is generally 25%, subject to applicable treaty relief and statutory exemptions. Qualifying distributions under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may be exempt where ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. A 12.8% rate generally applies to dividends paid to non-resident individuals, subject to treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Verify the recipient's tax residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, minimum participation, holding period, subject-to-tax status, and principal-purpose or anti-abuse conditions. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority before payment where possible. Apply the treaty rate at source only where French administrative requirements are satisfied; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and pursue a refund using the applicable French claim procedure. Retain residence certificates, ownership evidence, payment records, treaty analysis, and anti-abuse documentation. Treaty relief does not eliminate French reporting and remittance obligations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a French resident to a non-resident may generally be subject to a domestic withholding rate of 25%, subject to exemptions and treaty reduction. Interest paid to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax under ordinary domestic rules, although specific anti-abuse, low-tax-jurisdiction, related-party, or instrument-classification rules may apply. Tax treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 0% to 10% and may provide 0% withholding on ordinary interest, but the exact rate depends on the applicable treaty, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose provisions, and characterization of the payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150,000,000 of annual turnover or gross assets generally triggers the full French transfer-pricing documentation obligation, subject to statutory ownership, control, tax-group, and transaction conditions. The French master file and local file must be prepared and maintained when applicable. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups meeting the EUR 750,000,000 consolidated revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone economic substance regulation identical to the UAE or certain offshore regimes. Nevertheless, French anti-abuse principles, the general anti-abuse rule, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, permanent-establishment principles, transfer-pricing requirements, and principal-purpose testing can deny benefits or deductions where arrangements lack genuine commercial substance. A bonded trucking SARL should maintain French operational capacity, drivers or contracted transport capability, vehicles or fleet-control arrangements, customs and transport licenses, dispatch and GPS records, personnel or decision-making capacity, bank activity, customer contracts, and commercially consistent risk allocation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing revenue, fabricating freight costs, falsifying mileage or customs records, deducting fictitious invoices, using undeclared cash, or deliberately understating taxable profit or VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax reassessment, late-payment interest, surcharges generally ranging from 10% to 80%, and criminal prosecution. Tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, with aggravated cases potentially reaching seven years and EUR 3,000,000, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and directors may incur criminal liability, tax-officer liability for fraudulent or persistently unpaid taxes, civil damages, asset seizure, and management bans. A corporate veil is not automatically pierced, but personal liability may follow from intentional misconduct, gross mismanagement, fraud, or commingling. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require a specific judicial or criminal basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or claiming fictitious VAT invoices, manipulating intra-EU transport evidence, misclassifying domestic freight as exempt international transport, or participating in missing-trader arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, interest, penalties potentially up to 80% for fraudulent conduct, refusal of input-tax recovery, joint liability in statutory cases, and criminal sanctions for aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted for intentional participation or facilitation, face asset seizure and management restrictions, and bear civil or tax liability where personal misconduct is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Unauthorized diversion of bonded goods, broken or falsified seals, inaccurate transit declarations, unlicensed customs activity, missing discharge evidence, or use of vehicles outside authorized customs procedures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs duties, import VAT, interest, administrative fines, seizure or forfeiture of goods and vehicles, suspension or withdrawal of customs authorizations, and possible criminal customs prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company officers and operational managers may be personally prosecuted where they ordered, knowingly permitted, or negligently facilitated violations. Customs guarantees and personal or corporate financial liability may be called upon.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, inflated fleet leases, unsupported royalties, artificial financing costs, or shifting French transport profit to a foreign related party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income reassessment, withholding-tax exposure, interest, penalties, documentation penalties, and possible denial of deductions. Failure to provide required documentation may produce a presumptive or adverse assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil and tax liability for deliberate concealment or abusive arrangements. Criminal liability generally requires proof of intentional fraud or participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal French SARL with no genuine transport operations, no effective management, no commercial risk, pass-through invoicing, circular payments, or artificial treaty-routing arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of deductions, treaty benefits, parent-subsidiary exemption, interest deductions, or tax credits; recharacterization of income; reassessment and anti-abuse penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for fraudulent management, tax evasion, insolvency misconduct, or asset diversion. Management bans and personal restitution orders may arise; travel bans are case-specific and not an automatic consequence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify customers or beneficial owners, ignoring suspicious payment patterns, accepting unexplained third-party payments, falsifying transport documentation, or failing to file required suspicious-transaction reports where subject to AML obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory warnings, injunctions, administrative fines, professional-license consequences, account restrictions, and criminal sanctions where money laundering or terrorist financing is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be personally liable for knowing participation, facilitation, concealment, or serious compliance failures. Money-laundering convictions may result in imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and judicial restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, or service fees to a foreign recipient without withholding, remitting, reporting, or substantiating treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, interest, penalties, denial of treaty relief, and possible penalties for inaccurate or missing reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative may face personal financial liability in cases of fraudulent withholding-tax avoidance, deliberate non-compliance, or serious management fault, in addition to corporate liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Employment, payroll, and undeclared labor violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using undeclared drivers, misclassifying employees as contractors, underreporting wages, failing to make social-security declarations, or breaching working-time and transport safety rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Backdated social contributions, surcharges, labor penalties, loss of public support, administrative closure, and criminal sanctions for concealed work or serious safety breaches.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally prosecuted for concealed work, wage fraud, or serious health and safety failures, with fines, imprisonment, management bans, and civil compensation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Preferential payments, diversion of fleet assets, related-party transfers below market value, continued trading while insolvent, destruction of books, or failure to file for insolvency within the statutory period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Clawback of transactions, extension of liabilities to managers in cases of management fault, bankruptcy or liquidation sanctions, asset recovery, and possible criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may impose contribution to insufficient assets, personal restitution, management bans, director disqualification, and imprisonment for fraudulent bankruptcy or asset concealment. Travel bans require a specific judicial order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining false books, omitting liabilities, fabricating customer or customs documents, backdating contracts, or failing to preserve statutory accounting and transport records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, accounting and corporate-law penalties, evidentiary presumptions against the company, and criminal sanctions for forgery, use of forged documents, or obstruction of tax inspection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director and responsible officers may face criminal prosecution, civil damages, asset seizure, management bans, and imprisonment where intentional falsification or obstruction is proven.
